subject: Request: Executive signoff — 3yr price anchor & renewal protection (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Exec clearance for 3yr price anchor + renewal protection (Acme Health)

Team —

Quick summary: Acme Health (pilot customer -> enterprise conversion) is asking for a three‑year committed contract with a fixed price anchor for years 1–3, an annual uplift cap of 8% (compound), and a renewal protection clause that prevents unilateral price increases beyond the uplift cap in year 4 if they renew within 90 days. They are also requesting a larger up-front discount in year 1 (30% list) to align with their budget cycle; year 2+ would step to 18% then 12%.

Why this is urgent: legal wants to finalize the MAA before their board meeting on 2028‑04‑18. Deal desk approved a standard 12‑month anchor only and flagged the uplift cap and renewal protection as nonstandard. Acme’s procurement (Lydia Park) said this term is a gating item for their CFO signoff.

Numbers (ref attached ACME_Deal_Summary_v3.pdf):
- TCV (3yr base): $3,450,000
- Year1 ARR-equivalent (after discount): $780,000
- Requested first-year discount: 30%
- Proposed uplift cap: 8% p.a.

Ask: Exec signoff to allow the 3‑year price anchor + 8% uplift cap and renewal protection, contingent on: (1) standard security attestation, (2) a no‑rebate clause if they terminate early, and (3) inclusion of a volume-based minimum utilization SLA. If you’re OK, we’ll route through legal for final MAA language.

Attachments: ACME_Deal_Summary_v3.pdf, uplift_scenario_table.xlsx, preliminary MAA draft.

Thanks —
Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec clearance for 3yr price anchor + renewal protection (Acme Health)

Michael —

Thanks for the clean summary. A few operational guardrails I’d want in addition to your contingencies before I recommend approval to the exec committee: 

1) Define a clear usage minimum per year (we proposed 60% of committed tokens in the Deal Summary). If utilization falls below that for two consecutive quarters, we retain the right to re‑price on a pro‑rata basis.
2) Include a hard cap on total cumulative discount impact (so the uplift cap doesn’t cascade with other rebates).
3) Escalation path: if a renewal negotiation goes beyond 45 days, the uplift cap expires and we revert to list price + standard discount table.

If legal can take the MAA and insert these clauses, I’m comfortable endorsing a one‑time exception to the deal desk for the 3yr anchor and 8% cap.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Exec clearance for 3yr price anchor + renewal protection (Acme Health)

On Thu, Apr 5, 2028 at 11:02 AM Marissa Cole wrote:
> If legal can take the MAA and insert these clauses, I’m comfortable endorsing a one‑time exception to the deal desk for the 3yr anchor and 8% cap.

Team —

Legal has reviewed a first pass (attached MAA_draft_20280409.docx). Key legal asks: they want a clearer termination remedy (we accepted your no‑rebate clause) and they recommend a 30‑day cure period for any material breach tied to usage minimums. They also advise against language that would lock us out from offering a better price to other customers (we can include a MFN carveout limited to the life of the agreement).

From a procurement/finance perspective I want a conditional approval:
- Approve 3yr anchor + 8% uplift cap provided we get CFO signoff on the final payment schedule and secure a 12‑month minimum commitment payment up front (prepayment credit applied to year1).

If Laura is good with the overall economics, please confirm and I’ll classify this for exec signoff.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

+1 on Marissa/Kim’s guardrails. A couple of commercial checks from my side:
- Confirm there’s a clause preventing aggregation of promotional discounts (we don’t want stacked credits).
- For reporting, require a quarterly utilization report delivered to our CS team; failure to produce allows us to pause discounts.

If Laura is comfortable with the prepayment + cure period + reporting obligations, I think this is reasonable to take to the exec for signoff.

—Jordan

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Request: Exec clearance for 3yr price anchor + renewal protection (Acme Health)

Team —

I’ve reviewed the summary, legal redline, and the finance memo. Given Acme Health’s strategic value and the speed to deployment, I approve a limited exception:

Decision (executive clearance granted):
- Approve 3‑year price anchor with an 8% annual uplift cap.
- Approve renewal protection clause as drafted, provided the renewal is executed within 90 days of term end.
- Require 12‑month prepayment applied to year1 and a quarterly utilization report to remain eligible for the discounted schedule.
- Include a 30‑day cure period for material breaches and a no‑stacking clause for promotions.

Conditions: final MAA to include the language Marissa and Kimberly requested and a single signatory escalation path if utilization falls short. Legal to complete and procurement to confirm payment schedule before DocuSign routing.

Please move forward. Laura

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
